text:
ella_cs: Quick help pls — AcroLabs onboarding. Getting a burst of 429s during deploy warmup. They run Node Lambda with our SDK (v0.8.3) and call initialize() inside the handler; when a canary or warmup runs they spin up ~12 concurrent invocations and immediate fanout. 429s spike for ~15-25s after deploy. Any short checklist?

raj_engineer: Ask for example request-ids + headers. Typical causes: parallel ephemeral token refresh / preflight fanout, or SDK init race that doesn't honor local cache/backoff.

ella_cs: Customer logs (sanitized):

```
2024-06-21T09:41:02Z req=rz1 POST /v1/chat 200
2024-06-21T09:41:03Z req=rz2 POST /v1/chat 429 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0
2024-06-21T09:41:03Z req=rz3 POST /v1/chat 429 X-RateLimit-Remaining:0
```

sam_platform: Yup warmup stampede. Which auth flow? Ephemeral tokens?

ella_cs: Yes, they're fetching ephemeral JWTs from an internal auth service per-instance.

raj_engineer: Two immediate client-side fixes to recommend: 1) Serialize token fetch on cold-starts — set PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 (or implement a single-flight fetch). 2) Add tiny randomized init jitter (0-300ms) before calling initialize() so instances don't all hit at the same ms. Also advise upgrading SDK to v0.9.x which contains a fix for concurrent-init backoff.

maria_ops: Also mention using the SDK's ephemeralTokenCache option to share tokens per-container (avoids repeated refreshes during the container lifetime). If they control warmup tooling, warm a single helper process and proxy requests to it.

ella_cs: Can you paste a 2-line blurb I can send to their SRE with concrete commands/envs?

raj_engineer: Send this: "Actionable mitigation: (1) Upgrade to Node SDK v0.9+; (2) set PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 during deploy warmups to serialize preflight; (3) enable ephemeralTokenCache in the SDK to reuse tokens per container; (4) add randomized init jitter (0-300ms) before Redwood.initialize(). Example: 

```
const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random()*300);
await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,jitter));
await Redwood.initialize({ ephemeralTokenCache: true });
```

These reduce short-window concurrent token creates and should eliminate the transient 429s without server changes."

ella_cs: Sent to customer. They applied PREFETCH_CONCURRENCY=1 + jitter and reported 95% fewer 429s immediately. They want a short doc entry for serverless onboarding.

maria_ops: I'll add a short note to the onboarding playbook and link to the SDK upgrade note.

sam_platform: I'll open an internal ticket to track the v0.8.3 concurrent-init backoff bug and add a proactive nudge for new customers on serverless.

infra-bot: Incident bot: Created ticket CS-8921 to follow up on SDK upgrade nudges.

ella_cs: Closing for now — will re-open if upgrade doesn't finish next week. Thanks all :tada:
